headline: RT by @sentdefender: Per an anonymous source, Mexican authorities discovered a suspected large-scale fuel theft (huachicol) network operating in Nuevo León, allegedly involving members of the National Guard and individuals linked to the Cartel del Noreste (CDN). According to the information, companies identified as Azamas and JRM were allegedly involved in transporting stolen fuel from a Pemex distribution facility in Cadereyta. The alleged network reportedly came under scrutiny following a dispute over corruption payments at the facility. A National Guard commander allegedly deserted, leaving behind a cellphone containing records of payments made to facilitate the extraction of stolen fuel. Authorities are reportedly conducting an internal search for the missing commander and a deserting soldier. The allegations identify Brigadier General Víctor Manuel Lemarroy Santos, Nuevo León State Coordinator of the National Guard, as the highest-ranking official allegedly connected to the network.

headline: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) has issued an update on operations against Iran in the region. The update says that nearly 4,000 ships have passed through the strait, with U.S. support, including 1.7 billion barrels of crude oil "since summer", reiterating that primary transit routes are clear of sea mines. CENTCOM also reports that "nearly 150" ships have been redirected, with 5 noncompliant vessels disabled, in support of the U.S. naval blockade of Southern Iran, preventing an estimated $30 billion in crude oil exports. The blockade has also been complemented by the recently established Task Force-Iron Gate (TF-IG) to "synchronize efforts to stop illicit movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illegal revenue streams" along Iran's land borders and Caspian Sea coastline.
